dedupe_keys.name: modelling flood defence failure at national scale and in wainfleet england jba risk management

description: This case study from JBA Risk Management, the flood modelling company, shows how its UK Flood Model treats flood defence failure and reports the effect on losses nationally and locally through a case study of Wainfleet in Lincolnshire. It defines three defence scenarios, undefended, overtopping, and overtopping with breach, and explains that failure probability combines each defence's standard of protection, defence type such as embankment or wall, and material condition with event water depths. Modelled as undefended, losses are 195 percent higher than with overtopping, while adding breaches raises losses only slightly, backed by evidence that only four breaches occurred over about 1,000 kilometres of defences tested in summer 2007 and seven in the 2015 to 2016 storms. JBA lowered the Environment Agency fragility curves accordingly. Coverage: United Kingdom, with one town in detail. Access: a free web article; the licence is not stated, and the model itself is commercial. Caveats: produced by the model vendor, with results shown as figures, not downloadable data. It supports defence fragility, exposure and resilience modelling, and relates to the JBA flood map data record and the Dutch Delta Programme case study in the catalogue.
